story_text:
## En français
Vigeos veille sur votre parent, chez lui. Une box et une caméra sont posées dans son logement : si la box repère une chute, vous recevez une alerte sur votre téléphone, avec un court extrait vidéo chiffré de bout en bout. Votre parent n'a rien à porter.
Je m'appelle Romain Dellamonica et je développe Vigeos seul, à Marseille, depuis fin 2025. Mes grands-parents habitent loin et se sont déjà blessés. Si personne n'avait été là à ce moment, nous ne l'aurions probablement pas su à temps.
Rien ne démarre sans l'accord de votre parent. Pas de reconnaissance faciale, pas d'écoute.
Vigeos est un prototype qui fonctionne, et la détection de chute est en bêta. Votre contribution finance la suite : les essais chez des familles, le boîtier définitif, la fabrication et le marquage CE.
L'offre :
- Kit box + 1 caméra : 349 € pour les 20 premiers contributeurs, puis 399 €. 429 € avec 2 caméras, 459 € avec 3.
- Abonnement : 6 premiers mois offerts au lieu de 29,99 €/mois, soit 179,94 € d'économie, et les 5 €/mois de chaque caméra en plus sont aussi offerts pendant ces 6 mois. Ensuite 29,99 €/mois, sans engagement de durée, plus 5 €/mois par caméra au-delà de la première.
- Livraison estimée en septembre 2027, après le marquage CE. Frais de port en plus : 10 € en France.
- Tout ou rien : votre carte n'est débitée que si l'objectif de 30 000 € est atteint d'ici le 14 décembre.
La suite de la page est en anglais. Une question ? Écrivez-moi en français.
## Real prototype demo: one continuous take
This is the real Vigeos prototype, filmed on October 7, 2026 in one continuous take, with no cuts: a team member sets up the box and camera with the app, simulates a fall, and the alert and encrypted video clip reach the family app. The phone's screen recording runs side by side, in sync. Waiting times are sped up (x2 to x16, shown on screen) and the clock in the corner shows the real elapsed time (6 min 54 s). Push notifications were silenced on this phone, so the alert is seen in the app's list. Fall detection is in beta.
It all started with a simple question: how do you protect older people who live alone without watching over them all the time?
In late 2025, I started building Vigeos, an AI-based fall detection system designed to run entirely at home. No button to press, no device to wear: just discreet technology that keeps watch.
What makes Vigeos different? The AI runs locally, right on the device. Your video clips are end-to-end encrypted. Your privacy is not a compromise, it is a right.
Render: concept of the final kit. The current prototype is shown in the photos and videos on this page.
After months of development and prototyping, Vigeos runs today as a working prototype on my bench. It has not been tested in a family's home yet: that is the next step, and this campaign will fund it. This Kickstarter campaign is not just a fundraiser, it is an invitation to join a mission: giving older people and their families the peace of mind they deserve.
## Where Vigeos stands today (October 2026)
Working on the prototype today: the home box (Raspberry Pi 5 with an AI accelerator, in my 3D-printed enclosure with a 5-inch screen), cameras running our own open firmware, the Vigeos family app (iOS beta) and the online service that delivers alerts to the app.
In development, and funded by this campaign: the fall detection model trained for real homes, inactivity alerts generated by the box, push notifications, the final enclosure, production and CE certification.
The photos below are unretouched pictures of the prototype as it is today, and the app video was recorded in a single unedited take. I will document every step in the project updates.
Current prototype: the 3D-printed home box with its 5-inch screen (screen off). Unretouched photo, October 2026.
Current prototype, side view: USB-C power input and ventilation. Unretouched photo, October 2026.
Current prototype, inside: Raspberry Pi 5 with the Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ (Hailo, 13 TOPS) and the screen cable. Unretouched photo, October 2026.
That was before I designed the final box that is shown in the photos.
Here is the newly designed prototype in a beautiful image

## Pricing and shipping
The kit (Vigeos box + 1 camera) is €399, or €429 with 2 cameras and €459 with 3 cameras. Every reward includes your first 6 months of subscription free, instead of €29.99/month: you save €179.94, and the €5/month for each additional camera is also free during those 6 months. After that, €29.99/month, no minimum term, plus €5/month for each camera beyond the first. Extra cameras are also available as add-ons for €30 each.
We ship worldwide. Shipping costs depend on your country and are added to your pledge at checkout. Estimated delivery: third quarter of 2027, after CE marking of the box and camera.
Vigeos is technology in the service of safety, with respect and dignity.

The Creator is solely responsible for complying with industry standards and applicable laws, including product safety standards. Vigeos is built by a single founder and, like any hardware project, it carries real risks. Here is how we see them and how we plan to handle them. Fall detection accuracy No AI system catches every fall. Our model is still being trained and validated, and real homes vary a lot: lighting, furniture, camera placement. Vigeos complements human care and emergency services; it does not replace them. Before shipping, we will test the system in real living conditions and share the results we actually measure. Manufacturing and delivery The kit is built from off-the-shelf components: a small home server and cameras running open firmware. Component shortages or supplier delays could push back the estimated delivery date (third quarter of 2027, after CE marking). If the schedule changes, we will tell you early and explain why. A small team Vigeos is currently developed by its founder alone. The funds raised will secure production, testing and customer support. An extended absence on my side could delay deliveries. Privacy and regulation Vigeos handles sensitive information about older people. The system is designed around the GDPR: video is processed locally at home and clips are end-to-end encrypted, so our servers never see them. Regulations may still evolve and require changes to the product or the service. Service continuity Alerts and remote access rely on our online service, hosted in Europe, with monitoring and encrypted backups. If the service ever had to stop, we commit to notifying users well in advance. We will post regular updates throughout the campaign and production, including the setbacks.
